A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Affogato dataset, annotation pipeline and Espresso models. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring and renaming.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-quality evaluation, quantitative 2D and 3D grounding experiments, background-augmentation ablations and partial-view experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original grounding experiments, human validation, pretraining comparisons, filtering controls, scaling and resolution analyses, and qualitative robot-scene evaluation.

M1.justification: The documented Espresso-3D objective changes from equally weighted Focal and Dice losses to BCE and Dice losses (v1 Appendix A.2; v2 Appendix B.2). Section 4 also changes frozen encoders to fine-tuned encoders, although v2 Appendix B.2 still states that the vision backbone is frozen, leaving the actual policy unresolved. The core architectures and three-stage annotation pipeline remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds qualitative zero-shot evaluation on cluttered Open X-Embodiment robot-workspace images (Figure 7) and removes the Affogato-Partial evaluation of partially observed furniture objects (v1 Appendix C). The principal Objaverse-derived, LASO and AGD20K coverage remains. Affogato-750K renames the existing annotation collection rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: The LASO comparison expands beyond OpenAD and PointRefer to include Referring Transformer, 3D-SPS, ReLA and IAGNet (v2 Table 2). AffordanceNet, associated with RAGNet, is added to both zero-shot and supervised AGD20K comparisons (Table 4). These are substantive additions to the reported comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 replaces direct LASO–Affogato transfer comparisons with LASO seen/unseen comparisons using pretraining followed by target-dataset fine-tuning. It adds category-filtering, training-volume and point-resolution controls. Human validation now describes disjoint annotator assignments and removal of incorrect queries. The reported 2D image count falls from 300,208 to 150,104, consistent with retaining only the most visible viewpoint instead of also sampling a neighboring view.

E4.justification: v2 adds held-out-category filtering, pretraining-scale and volume-matching analyses, training/test resolution sensitivity, qualitative CoT and mask-selection ablations, and stage-specific failure analysis (Section 5.4; Appendix C). These investigate overlap, scaling, design choices and error mechanisms previously untested. The partial-view robustness study is removed; the background-augmentation ablation remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added scores and failure percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation or change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for pretraining, new comparators and controls; its new LASO comparison reports Espresso-3D unseen aIoU of 18.7 without versus 20.8 with pretraining. Human validation changes from 72.3% good, 12.3% ok and 15.4% not good to 84.8% success with an error breakdown. Direct cross-dataset and partial-view results disappear. Retained Affogato and Espresso-2D scores match after accounting for percentage rescaling.

T1.justification: Neither version provides theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive derivations. The coverage and diversity definitions remain equivalent, and the added empirical analyses introduce no new formal theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain automated large-scale affordance annotation and unified 2D/3D grounding. v2 explicitly extends the pretraining-benefit claim to prior architectures and emphasizes gains on unseen categories. It drops v1's explicit claim of being the first to integrate the separate 2D and 3D research streams.

C2.justification: v2 interprets filtered-pretraining gains as evidence beyond category overlap, attributes cross-domain asymmetry primarily to training volume, and explains early 2D saturation through the synthetic-to-real domain gap. It adds substantive CoT, mask-selection and error-propagation explanations. v1's frozen-encoder rationale, detailed critique of prior heatmaps and partial-view robustness discussion are removed. Existing background and action-detail limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents smallest-mask selection, category-filtering instructions, explicit instance/view/query separation, and interpolation when training and test resolutions differ. It adds a project-page link while retaining the dataset URL. Model checkpoints, hardware, training budgets and most implementation recipes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of 2HandedAfforder, RAGNet, LMAffordance3D and recent 2D-to-3D transfer work. It acknowledges automated large-scale 2D datasets and contrasts their single-view supervision with multi-view aggregation. These update the competitive context while retaining the underlying positioning around affordance-data scarcity and open-vocabulary coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Separate 2D/3D related-work discussions are consolidated, Affogato becomes the framework name and Affogato-750K the dataset name, a dedicated analysis subsection is introduced, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The overview and pipeline diagrams are redrawn, the prior-dataset failure figure is replaced by human-validation and pipeline-error displays, and several analysis tables and figures are added. Tables are reorganized around pretraining comparisons. The former zero-shot Figure 7 moves to Appendix Figure A4, selected supervised examples move into Figure 9, and partial-view displays are removed. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1's main 3D evidence for dataset utility relied on cross-dataset performance gaps. v2 directly tests pretraining benefits across architectures and checks held-out-category overlap (Tables 2 and 5), substantially strengthening the central empirical argument. Scaling, volume controls and pipeline-error analysis further improve validation. The contradictory encoder-training descriptions in Section 4 and Appendix B.2 impair reproducibility, and partial-view validation is lost, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger evidence for the dataset's principal contribution.
